title: Mekhi and the Dawgs: The League's Sharpest Football Mind, Forever Drafting From the Wrong Time Zone
body: Every league needs a franchise loyalist, and Mekhi has never run anything but the Dawgs. Kai is probably the best pure football brain in the Buckaroo Football League, which makes his record one of the great mysteries of modern fantasy science. He opened in 2023 with a 6-8 season, 1542.8 points, a 4 seed and a fourth-place finish. Respectable, quiet, and with nine pickups, a hint of the waiver-wire habit to come.

2024 was the dip: 5-9, 1413.5 points, a 5 seed and fifth place. It also produced the low point of his career, a 67.9-point dud in week 14 against Randy. Kai made zero trades in each of his first two seasons, a man who apparently believed the answers were on the waiver wire and nowhere else. History suggests he may have been half right.

Then came 2025, the strangest season of his career. Mekhi drafted from basic training, which is a tough setting for a mock draft, and still put up a career-best 1858.2 points and an 8-8 record, good for the 4 seed. In week 9 he hung a franchise-record 153.6 on Randy, a fitting revenge for the 2024 disaster. Somehow that same season ended with the Dawgs in sixth of six, the last-place spot that Sonny had just escaped. Going .500 with a playoff seed and still taking last is a feat that would make a statistician weep, and his career playoff record sits at 0-1.

The head-to-head ledger tells the rest. Randy is his truest rival at a dead-even 6-6, and both the best and worst nights of Kai's career came against him. Kaushal is the nemesis: Habib has beaten the Dawgs eight times in ten tries, and the 2-8 mark suggests the two-time champ checks Mekhi's spot on the schedule first. Brucie leads him 3-6, Philliberto holds a 4-6 villain's edge, and Sonny sits up 5-7. The good news: Kai is a perfect 1-0 against both JMoney and Zilgit, so the newcomers have been warned.

Which brings us to 2026, a season Mekhi drafted from overseas, extending the worst draft-day timing streak in the league. The Dawgs sit at 2-4 with 642.4 points and 5% title odds, but don't count out the waiver-wire king: he has already made eight pickups and one trade, matching his entire 2025 pickup total in six weeks. With 31 career pickups and counting, Kai keeps working the margins like a man who knows something the rest of us don't. Someday the football knowledge and the results are going to line up, and the rest of the league should hope it isn't this year.
